 Print Arijit Singh and Diljit Dosanjh are gearing up for major India tours, but fans hoping to catch the singers live will face a stark difference in ticket prices. While Arijit’s most expensive concert package is priced at Rs 11.8 lakh, Diljit’s top ticket costs Rs 18,000. Both artists are set to begin their respective tours at Ahmedabad’s Narendra Modi Stadium, although their approaches to concert pricing differ considerably. Arijit has announced a nine-city India tour in 2027 to celebrate 20 years in the music industry. The concerts are expected to feature some of his biggest hits, including ‘Agar Tum Saath Ho’, ‘Tum Hi Ho’ and ‘Vida Karo’. The announcement comes months after the singer revealed in January that he would step away from playback singing to focus on his independent musical pursuits. Watch Vishal Bhardwaj shares throwback jamming video with Arijit Singh Scheduled to run from January to May 2027, the tour will offer tickets across a wide price range. Entry-level tickets for the Ahmedabad concert at Narendra Modi Stadium start at Rs 999, while the most expensive package, available at Mumbai’s Mahalaxmi Racecourse, costs Rs 11.8 lakh for a table accommodating 15 people. According to thumpN, the tour’s official ticketing partner, premium packages across cities are priced between Rs 7 lakh and Rs 10 lakh. Designed for groups seeking a more exclusive experience, these packages include couch seating, special gifts, premium alcohol bottles, dedicated entry and exit points, and separate lavatories. The luxury experience also extends to social media. Guests will have a dedicated content creator film an Instagram Reel featuring them at the concert, with the video shared the following day. Despite the steep prices, demand for the premium categories remains strong, with reports suggesting that around 60% of the top-priced options have already been sold. Arijit has witnessed similar demand in the past, with a 40-seater premium lounge at his Pune concert reportedly selling for Rs 16 lakh three years ago. The singer’s 2027 tour is expected to draw around five lakh people across nine cities. Ahmedabad will host the opening concert on January 9, followed by Chandigarh on January 23 and Jaipur on February 7. The tour will then move to Mumbai on February 20, Bengaluru on March 13 and New Delhi on March 27. Pune is scheduled for April 10, followed by Indore on May 1 and Hyderabad on May 15. Diljit Dosanjh, meanwhile, is preparing for the India leg of his ongoing Aura World Tour. Following the success of his 2024 Dil-Luminati Tour, which reportedly generated Rs 943 crore in revenue, the Punjabi singer is set to perform in several Indian cities. Unlike Arijit’s premium hospitality offerings, Diljit’s highest-priced tickets for the upcoming shows are capped at Rs 18,000, making the concert experience comparatively more accessible to fans. Diljit has been performing across Europe and North America as part of the Aura World Tour this year. The India leg will begin in Delhi-NCR on November 1, followed by Indore on November 15, Ahmedabad on November 21, Mumbai on November 27 and Bengaluru on November 29. He will then perform in Lucknow on December 5. A Chandigarh show has also been announced, although the promoter is yet to share further details. Arijit Singh first rose to prominence after participating in the reality show ‘Fame Gurukul’ in 2005. Over the years, he has become one of Hindi cinema’s most popular playback singers, delivering chartbusters such as ‘Gerua’, ‘Channa Mereya’, ‘Ae Dil Hai Mushkil’, ‘Bulleya’, ‘Naina’, ‘Zaalima’, ‘Galti Se Mistake’, ‘Ae Watan’, ‘Mast Magan’, ‘Rait Zara Si’, ‘Kesariya’, ‘Apna Bana Le’, ‘Jhoome Jo Pathaan’, ‘Tum Kya Mile’, ‘Ve Kamleya’, ‘Chaleya’, ‘Sajni’ and ‘Gehra Hua’. His more recent work includes ‘Jai Jai Ram’ from the upcoming Ranbir Kapoor-starrer ‘Ramayana’, which is scheduled for a Diwali 2026 release. Diljit Dosanjh, on the other hand, has built a successful career as both a singer and an actor over the past two decades. With a strong fan base in India and overseas, he has become known for his energetic live performances and large-scale concerts. He was most recently seen in Imtiaz Ali’s ‘Main Vaapas Aaunga’, alongside Naseeruddin Shah, Sharvari and Vedang Raina.
